title: Detecting Delirium in Older People: The Development of a Web-based Tool for Family Caregivers
content:
Background and Objectives: Delirium is a common neuropsychiatric syndrome in older adults, often identified by caregivers. However, there are currently no accessible tools for family caregivers in Thailand to detect delirium. This study aimed to develop a web-based tool, ‘delirium-detect,’ to assist caregivers in identifying delirium in older individuals. 
       Methods: A research and development approach was employed, involving literature reviews, expert and key informant interviews, focus groups, content validity assessments, and pilot testing. The final tool features a 22-item symptom checklist that guides caregivers in assessing delirium, available on both PCs and mobile devices in Thai and English. It also provides daily home care guidance and emphasizes early detection. Expert reviews confirmed high validity (content validity index of 1.00).        Results: All participants completed the questionnaires in a pilot test with 11 caregivers of older adults diagnosed with delirium, indicating criterion validity. The overall satisfaction was high, with 54.5% "liking" the tool and reporting ease of use. Participants spent an average of 9.09 minutes using the tool, with around 5 minutes for the questionnaire. 
        Conclusions: The ‘delirium-detect’ tool proved practical and user-friendly, highlighting its potential for early delirium detection in older adults. Further research is needed for broader implementation.
